subject: Social Media
title: The Loneliness Paradox
description: A 60-second lesson on The Loneliness Paradox.

hook.text: You feel lonely, so you open Instagram. You scroll for 30 minutes. You feel lonelier. The loop traps you.

buildup.text: Passive scrolling—viewing without interacting—is linked to increased loneliness and depression.

discovery.text: Active use—messaging, commenting, creating—can reduce loneliness. But most usage is passive consumption.

twist.text: Platforms profit from passive scrolling. It generates ad views. Active use is harder to monetize.

climax.text: The design encourages passive consumption. Frictionless scrolling, autoplay, and infinite feeds all reward passivity.

punchline.text: The app profits from your loneliness.

quiz.question: What type of social media use is linked to increased loneliness?
options: Active use like messaging and commenting
